Chapter 157: A Massive Valuation of $25 Million

After several days of waiting, Chen Guiliang finally saw Lin Dongliang and Fu Jixun arrive in Beijing again.

"Here is the latest data for Xiaonei Wang..."

"Also, two weeks ago, I fronted 300,000 yuan for Xiaonei Wang, which can be considered a debt owed by the site..."

Chen Guiliang took out the latest documents.

After the basic terms of the negotiation were settled, the investors would conduct comprehensive due diligence on these things.

Lin Dongliang ignored all that and asked instead, "Did you guess that Facebook would get funding recently?"

"Xiaonei Wang is benchmarked against Facebook, so of course I have to keep an eye on them at all times," Chen Guiliang said.

Fu Jixun asked, "So, you've been dragging your feet on the negotiations this whole time just to wait for Facebook?"

Chen Guiliang made no attempt to hide it. "Yes."

Lin Dongliang stopped beating around the bush and said directly, "According to the professional assessment by the teams from both IDG and DFJ, we've unanimously agreed that a valuation of $15 million for Bytedance is the most appropriate."

Chen Guiliang said, "Last year, IDG invested $2 million in Fenbei Wang, giving it a valuation of around $8 million to $10 million, right? Back then, Fenbei Wang hadn't even scammed that many song copyrights. Based on Xiaonei Wang's current scale and prospects, it's only worth a little more than Fenbei Wang?"

Lin Dongliang fell silent.

What else could he say?

Argue that it was another IDG partner who made that investment?

That $2 million investment in Fenbei Wang was very puzzling. IDG somehow only took a 20% stake.

At the time, Fenbei Wang was practically on the verge of bankruptcy, and its founder was even planning to shut down the site and look for a job. Who knows what the IDG investor was thinking.

Lin Dongliang carefully chose his words and said, "The investment in Fenbei Wang is part of IDG's strategic layout in China's music market, which includes, but is not limited to, Jiutian Music and Fenbei Wang. We've invested in several Chinese online music platforms."

"No matter the strategy, you still have to invest at market price," Chen Guiliang said. "If Xiaonei Wang's valuation is only this little bit more than Fenbei Wang's was last year, then I'm very sorry, but I will take it as an insult to myself and my team!"

"What valuation do you think is appropriate?" Fu Jixun asked.

Chen Guiliang made an outrageous demand, "Fifty million US dollars!"

"Haha." Fu Jixun laughed out of frustration.

Lin Dongliang said, "Mr. Chen, we came here with sincerity. We hope you can show some sincerity as well."

Chen Guiliang said, "Facebook had previously only received a few hundred thousand dollars in angel investment. Now, it has secured over $12 million in its Series A, giving it a post-money valuation of a hundred million dollars. Is it unreasonable for me to value my own company at fifty million? It's you who lacks sincerity by valuing it at fifteen million!"

Chen Guiliang's confidence now was much greater than it had been two months ago.

First, Xiaonei Wang's user base was growing at lightning speed, now approaching 1.9 million people. Furthermore, a series of activities had made the users increasingly active.

Second, the advertising business was growing. Ao Yanchen had specifically recruited advertising salespeople for this purpose. The number of ad slots had also increased from the initial three to the current twelve.

Third, Facebook's successful financing meant that even if IDG and DFJ didn't invest, other venture capitalists would come knocking later.

After a lot of back and forth, Lin Dongliang and Fu Jixun raised the valuation to $18 million.

Chen Guiliang firmly rejected it.

On the first day, the negotiations failed. They could not reach a consensus.

Back at the hotel, Lin Dongliang and Fu Jixun began their discussion.

Lin Dongliang muttered, "If I hadn't dragged it out for so long, and had negotiated the valuation two months ago, do you think we would've already signed an agreement?"

"What do you think? This fellow Chen deliberately dragged his feet, waiting for this very moment," Fu Jixun said.

Lin Dongliang said, "The valuation Chen Guiliang is asking for is too high. I need to discuss this with the founding partners."

Fu Jixun was also very curious. "What on earth were you guys thinking when you invested in Fenbei Wang? They didn't even have the copyrights to any popular songs back then, yet you invested $2 million for just a 20% stake. Normally, you could've achieved the same result with $500,000."

"That wasn't my investment!" Lin Dongliang emphasized.

"Hahaha."

Fu Jixun couldn't help but laugh, treating IDG like a big sucker.

The two men stepped away from each other to call their respective founding partners in China, then reconvened to discuss the next day's negotiations.

After five full days of haggling, they finally hammered out a general plan.

Bytedance's pre-money valuation was set at $25 million.

IDG would invest $3 million for a 10% stake.

DFJ would invest $2 million for a 6.6666% stake.

An option pool of 13.333% would be reserved. (Before the employees meet the vesting conditions, Chen Guiliang and Guo Feng will hold these options in trust. They can continue to hold them for a period after the company goes public.)

Chen Guiliang's stake would be 64.4%.

Guo Feng's stake would be 5.6%.

This was a relatively standard ownership structure for a Series A financing.

Some people might say that Ding Lei of NetEase still held 58.5% of the shares before its IPO, but that was because NetEase had only gone through two rounds of financing.

Chen Guiliang was confident that, just like Ding Lei, he could take the company public after only two funding rounds, and his pre-IPO shareholding would not be much different from Ding Lei's.

Even after going public, by holding employee options in trust initially, Chen Guiliang could control over 55% of the company's voting rights. Then, by finding opportunities to buy back shares, even after the employee options were vested, Chen Guiliang could still maintain effective control of over 50% of the voting rights. This was exactly what Ding Lei had done, except he had capitalized on the 2000 internet bubble, while Chen Guiliang planned to capitalize on the 2008 financial crisis.

In addition, Lin Dongliang and Fu Jixun also had Chen Guiliang add an anti-dilution clause.

This meant that if Bytedance's valuation decreased in the next funding round, IDG and DFJ had to be guaranteed against losses, with the founder's equity making up for the lost value.

As long as the company's valuation did not decrease, this clause would not be triggered.

After the financing, a three-person board of directors would be formed.

Chen Guiliang and Guo Feng would each have one board seat, and IDG would have one. For the time being, there would be no independent directors, but DFJ could recommend a finance professional.

It was specially noted that the venture capital firm's director would not have veto power.

If Chen Guiliang wanted to invest in or acquire other companies to complete his business strategy, and if such transactions involved share transfers, IDG and DFJ would have the right of first refusal. As long as Chen Guiliang and Guo Feng did not transfer their shares, this clause would not be triggered.

There were also restrictive clauses on subsequent financing. For instance, if Chen Guiliang made a huge acquisition that could only be funded by a Series B round, he would have to sign new restrictive clauses with IDG and DFJ during that round.

If an acquisition by Chen Guiliang significantly increased the risk for Bytedance, or caused a delay in the exit timeline for IDG and DFJ, the two venture capital firms would have the right to step in and block the acquisition.

There were numerous clauses and a huge pile of agreements.

This was currently a draft contract. After IDG and DFJ completed their second round of due diligence, a more formal and complete contract would be drafted. At that time, Chen Guiliang would hire professional lawyers to check for any loopholes.

During the due diligence period, the finance professional recommended by DFJ also arrived.

His name was Chang Zhongxiang, a man of about 40, who was about to become Bytedance's CFO.

Chen Guiliang could use him for the time being to build the company's financial system. If he felt Chang was a good fit, he would keep him on. If he felt something was off, he would find an opportunity to kick him out later.

Ao Yanchen and Xie Yang both signed their option contracts during this period. The term was for four years, with 25% vesting each year.

They would have to work at Bytedance for over four years and meet corresponding performance targets to be able to cash in their options a period after the company went public. If they left the company midway, Chen Guiliang could repurchase the options at a discounted price.

The two of them could certainly not fill the entire option pool. In the future, employees who made significant contributions would also sign option contracts.

Chen Guiliang also had to balance things on the Game Science side, otherwise, they would surely be disgruntled.

The employees of the two companies had previously been interchangeable, often being borrowed to help each other out. Now that Bytedance had received investment, its employees' compensation would surely increase, which would naturally make the employees at Game Science unhappy.

Chen Guiliang directly gave Dong Qianqiu 4% of Game Science's equity, which served both to win over Dong Qianqiu and to mitigate the restrictions and risks of a sole proprietorship.
